text.p: Saudi Arabia's Portugese coach has taken his side to the final of the Asian Cup with a very new style of football. He calls it the ''Saudi-style''.
The Saudis have always prided themselves that they play Brazilian-style, basing their game on highly skilled individuals blending well to produce entertaining football.
But coach Eduardo Vingada says he does not want to be restricted to a certain type of game.
''I have them play the Saudi style, why the Brazilian style?'' he told Reuters on Thursday.

''The Saudis have a different mentality, different society. I want to take out the best of the good things of these from the players and develope it into their own style on the field, not the Brazilian, not the Portugese,'' Vingada said.

The Saudis reached their fourth Asian Cup final in succession with a 4-3 penalty-shootout win over Iran after a goalless draw in extra time on Wednesday. They take on hosts the United Arab Emirates in the final in Abu Dhabi on Saturday.
Saudi Arabia won the competition in 1984 and 1988. They were beaten by Japan in the 1992 final.
The Saudis have produced some of the finest football of the tournament and with Japan and South Korea knocked out at the quarter-final stage, they are now the clear favourites to win a third title.
The former coach of the Portugese under-21 and Olympic teams took over the Saudi squad in early November after disappointing results in a regional competition in October.
His contract covers only the Asian Cup. He said he would discuss his future with Saudi football officials after the competition.
Asked if he would agree to stay on for the World Cup qualifiers starting in March, Vingada said: ''If they want me, only one word will be enough.''
He wants to build for the future.
''The average age of the squad is 23 or less...and they are improving all the time,'' Vingada said, adding that some of his players could play in top European clubs.

Playmaker Khalid Al-Muwalid showed real class at the begining of the tournament but struggled a bit in the knockout stage. Striker Fahad Al-Mahalel is a strong finisher who has four goals to his name in the tournament so far.
Goalkeeper Mohammed Daeyea and defenders Abdullah Zubrom have been rock solid at the back but the player who Vingada is most excited about is defender Hussain Sulaimani.
''He has been amazing for us, and he is only 19. This guy has a bright future,'' he said.

Saudi Arabia's Asian Cup preperations were rocked when their star player Saeed Al-Oweiran -- who scored a great individual goal against Belgium in the 1994 World Cup -- and two other squad candidates were suspended.
The trio were said to have been found at a party drinking and mixing with women. Both are banned in Saudi Arabia under the Islamic sharia law.
